record.original_question: If x and y are positive integers with y^2 != x^3, is it always true that |y^2 - x^3| >= C max(y^2, x^3)^(1/6) for some absolute constant C > 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.7 (Hall). If x and y are positive integers with y 2 6= x3 , then |y 2 − x3 | ≥ C max{y 2 , x3 }1/6 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C>0$ be an absolute constant. Prove or disprove: there exists such a constant $C$ with the property that for every pair of positive integers $x,y$ satisfying $y^2 \neq x^3$, one has
$$|y^2 - x^3| \;\geq\; C \cdot \max\{y^2,\, x^3\}^{1/6}.$$
Equivalently, determine whether the gap between perfect squares and perfect cubes (when nonzero) is bounded below by a constant times the sixth root of the larger of the two.
artifact.category_tag: Hall's conjecture on squares and cubes
artifact.status_search_result: Hall's conjecture (in this strong form with exponent 1/6) is widely regarded as a famous open problem. Computational searches (notably by Elkies and later extensions) have found many examples with |y^2 - x^3| as small as roughly c·x^(1/2), suggesting the conjectured exponent 1/6 may be best possible, but no proof or disproof is known. A weaker form follows conditionally from the ABC conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Hall's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Hall's conjecture states that for nonzero |y^2 - x^3|, the difference is bounded below by a constant times max(x^3,y^2)^{1/6}; the conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Hall's conjecture is still an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Elkies, Rational points near curves and small nonzero |x^3 - y^2| via lattice reduction
status_evidence.snippet: Provides large computational searches for small values of |x^3 - y^2| relevant to Hall's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical evidence supports the exponent 1/6 but no proof exists.
